risks.note: EBITDA margin was 0.41%, 0.46% and 0.30% and profit for the year margin 0.37%, 0.34% and 0.22% in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 on revenue from operations of ₹941,862.12 million, ₹662,307.79 million and ₹349,214.93 million. The RHP states that given thin operating margins, even limited disruptions in hedging effectiveness, execution timing, liquidity conditions or counterparty performance during a sharp price correction may have a disproportionate adverse effect on EBITDA, profitability, net worth and cash flows, and that a decline in gold or silver prices reduces reported revenues one-for-one.
risks.risk: Structurally thin operating margins on very large gross revenue, with revenue directly linked to metal prices

risks.note: Operations require high working capital because funds are needed to purchase gold and silver, which are expensive commodities. RBI circulars and directions restrict the Company's access to debt financing for working capital; total borrowings were only ₹126.72 million with debt to equity of 0.01 times at March 31, 2026, and ₹4,650.00 million of Net Proceeds is earmarked for working capital. Inability to access adequate and cost-effective funding in a timely manner would adversely affect operations, liquidity and financial performance.
risks.risk: Working-capital intensity combined with an inability to access bank debt financing

risks.note: The top 10 customers accounted for 52.09%, 35.72% and 36.63% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024; the top 5 for 46.32%, 28.89% and 29.43%; and the largest single customer for 27.44%, 11.90% and 12.17%. The largest customer in Fiscals 2026 and 2025 was Riddisiddhi Bullions Limited, a Promoter Group member and Group Company (₹258,474.29 million in Fiscal 2026). No long-term agreements are executed with any customer.
risks.risk: Severe and worsening customer concentration, with the largest customer being a Promoter Group entity

risks.note: The absolute sum of all related party transactions was ₹457,141.31 million, ₹244,390.98 million and ₹95,216.21 million in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024; related party income items alone were 27.27%, 11.95% and 8.80% of revenue from operations. risks.risk: Extensive related-party dependence and potential conflicts of interest

risks.note: 'Augmont SPOT' generated 86.80%, 83.56% and 91.17% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, and the business activity falls under one reported segment, gold refining and trading. The Company primarily conducts business through two self-owned online platforms, so any significant disruption in IT systems or breach of data security would directly affect revenue and reputation.
risks.risk: Revenue concentration in a single platform and a single business vertical

risks.note: Capacity utilisation was 0.93% at Rudrapur (144 MTPA installed) and 8.53% at Mumbai (140 MTPA installed) in Fiscal 2026, with Rudrapur utilisation having fallen from 8.58% in Fiscal 2024. The RHP flags under-utilisation of manufacturing and refining facilities as a risk factor, while noting that utilisation is directly related to the strategy of choosing between refining and purchasing pure bars.

Business depends on continuous and cost-effective procurement of gold and silver, subject to global commodity price volatility, foreign exchange movements, changes in import duties and tariffs, evolving bullion-trade regulation, geopolitical tensions, sanctions and export controls affecting bullion-exporting countries. The economics of refining rest on a 0.65% lower import duty on dore bars versus refined gold, a policy-set spread outside the Company's control.
risks.risk: Dependence on procurement continuity and on the imported dore bar duty differential

risks.note: Operations require numerous approvals from DGFT, BIS, GST authorities, customs and securities market regulators; the digital gold business of Material Subsidiary Augmont Goldtech Private Limited operates in an unregulated space; hedging is exposed to counterparty and exchange systemic risk; and the Company is exposed to theft and fraud, hazardous refining and manufacturing processes, and government measures or public appeals discouraging gold purchases.
risks.risk: Regulatory intensity, hedging and operational-integrity exposure across a licence-heavy gold value chain

anomalies.detail: Installed refining capacity is 144 MTPA (Rudrapur) + 140 MTPA (Mumbai) as of March 31, 2026, both described as gold AND silver refining units. No silver refined volume is printed, and no utilisation percentage appears anywhere for any unit or year, so the apparent gap CANNOT be quantified from this RHP without deriving a number it does not print — and any gold-only ratio against a gold-and-silver capacity would be scope-mismatched as well as derived. The commercial reading the RHP itself supports is that refining is a small part of the business: cost of materials consumed (explicitly 'the cost of the doré bars that we import and other unrefined gold and silver for our refining operations') was 21.96% of total income in Fiscal 2026 against purchases of stock in trade ('the cost of the refined gold and silver that we buy and sell to customers') at 77.59% — i.e. the business is overwhelmingly a TRADING business by cost, with refining a minority input. Doré bars procured also fell over the period on the RHP's own volumes: 14.97 MT in Fiscal 2024 to 10.78 MT in Fiscal 2026, and scrap gold 6.62 MT in Fiscal 2025 to 3.49 MT in Fiscal 2026. Flagged for the verdict step: the absence of ANY capacity-utilisation table is itself notable for a company with three stated manufacturing/refining units and a Net Proceeds object that includes expanding refining.

business_ops.supply_chain_integration:
The issuer describes itself as 'an integrated gold and silver platform in India serving businesses and consumers, with a presence across 24 states, as of March 31, 2026', whose 'operations span across multiple segments of the gold and silver value chain including procurement and refining, bullion trading, digital gold offerings, jewellery manufacturing, international sales and facilitating gold-backed financial services.'

BACKWARD INTEGRATION (upstream). Procurement runs through four disclosed channels: refined gold and silver bought from Indian and international banks; doré bars imported and refined in-house, which the RHP quantifies as carrying import duties 'lower ... by 0.65% as compared to directly importing refined gold'; scrap gold and silver bought from individuals, jewellers and at jewellery auctions 'at reduced rates'; and refined metal imported through the IIBX via the GIFT City subsidiary Augmont IFSC Private Limited, where the issuer 'execute[s] transactions directly as a trading member', saving 'expenses associated with brokerage and commission', and where 'the gold is procured from sources such as LBMA-accredited refiners or UAE Good Delivery-accredited refiners'. The issuer then owns the refining step itself, through two units (Rudrapur 144 MTPA and Mumbai 140 MTPA as of March 31, 2026) with in-house NABL/ISO-IEC-17025:2017-accredited assaying laboratories and BIS hallmarking licences, certified under India Good Delivery standards and authorised to deliver refined bullion on BSE- and MCX-operated commodity exchanges.

MANUFACTURING. A jewellery manufacturing unit at Sitapur SEZ, Jaipur, Rajasthan (13.80 MTPA installed capacity as of March 31, 2026) converts metal into gold jewellery articles, primarily chains, for the international sales business.

FORWARD INTEGRATION (downstream). The issuer owns and operates both of its distribution platforms — 'Augmont SPOT' for enterprise customers (operational since 2012, 5,223 registered members) and 'Augmont Gold For All' for consumers (launched Fiscal 2021) — and owns the price-discovery layer on the enterprise side ('our pricing engine monitors these inputs through a combination of our in-house technology, AI powered tools and human oversight ... live tracking, predictive analysis and efficient hedging strategies'; 'we do not charge users of our platform any brokerage or terminal fees and we include our margins in the prices that are quoted on our platform'). Physical last-mile is partly owned and partly outsourced: of 20 spot delivery centres across 13 states, nine are operated directly and 11 through franchisees, with delivery 'typically fulfilled within two working days'.

WHERE INTEGRATION STOPS — THIRD-PARTY AND RELATED-PARTY DEPENDENCE. The consumer physical network is NOT owned: all 106 Gold-For-All centres are 'operated by Finkurve', a Group Company, and the issuer 'maintain[s] an asset light structure at these centers as they do not carry physical inventory'. Gold lending is not undertaken by the issuer at all — under a service level agreement dated June 1, 2024 (effective July 1, 2024) it only 'provide[s] technology, marketing and brand support through our platform for gold loans provided by' Finkurve. Consumer reach otherwise depends on third parties: 'over 218 partners such as Gullak, and Candere' for order placement, Kalyan Jewellers and CaratLane for physical redemption of digital gold, 3,700 Muthoot Fincorp branches for investment jewellery (a Technopak-sourced figure), an unnamed NBFC's stores, 705 independent financial agents, and third-party payment gateways for collections. The issuer states the synergy rationale itself: 'the gold and silver that we procure for selling on our 'Augmont SPOT' platform, helps us with our raw material requirements for manufacturing jewellery as well as for the other products and services that we provide through our consumer-focused business, thereby serving multiple business verticals', alongside centralised 'finance, information technology, strategy and procurement' functions.

STATED EXPANSION OF THE CHAIN. ₹ 4,650.00 million of the Net Proceeds is proposed to be used 'towards funding future working capital requirements towards procurement of raw material, maintenance of inventory and funding advance margin requirements for procurement purposes'; 15 new spot delivery centres are planned in Tier 3 and Tier 4 cities by Fiscal 2029; the issuer intends to fund 'minimum order quantity commitments under long-term supply arrangements our Company may enter with miners, in Fiscals 2027, 2028 and 2029'; and it 'also propose[s] to expand our refining op' — the routed extract is cut off mid-sentence at that point, so the refining-expansion plan itself is NOT in the provided extract.

Repayable in equated monthly instalments over a 36-month tenor. Lender names are not disclosed anywhere: the Financial Indebtedness statement is presented by CATEGORY of borrowing, not loan-by-loan or lender-by-lender.

overview.business_model: The Company operates two business verticals through distinct online platforms, complemented by a physical distribution network. (i) Enterprise and international sales: the 'Augmont SPOT' platform, a fully electronic over-the-counter delivery-based bullion platform operational since 2012, enables GST-registered jewellers, bullion dealers and manufacturers to buy gold and silver bars online with assured physical delivery through 20 spot delivery centres across 13 states as of March 31, 2026 (nine operated directly, 11 through franchisees), with deliveries typically fulfilled within two working days; the Company also sells gold bullion to asset management companies in exchange for gold ETF units and trades in gold and silver ETF units. Augmont SPOT had over 5,223 registered members as of March 31, 2026 and generated revenue of ₹817,505.69 million in Fiscal 2026 (86.80% of revenue from operations), of which gold sales were ₹647,580.59 million (49.13 MT) and silver ₹169,925.10 million (1,033.57 MT). International sales comprise the manufacture and sale of gold jewellery articles, primarily chains, to jewellery customers. (ii) Consumer-focused offerings through the 'Augmont Gold For All' platform and offline channels, enabling consumers to buy, sell and store gold and silver digitally, purchase gold through systematic investment plans, liquidate and sell old gold, and purchase jewellery starting from 1 gm; this platform generated ₹30,120.51 million in Fiscal 2026 (3.20% of revenue from operations). financial_valuation.detail: The Company procures, refines and trades gold and silver bullion and jewellery, so metal-price volatility affects both product demand and inventory valuation. It states it generally does not maintain large bullion inventories in the ordinary course, but must hold metal for longer periods due to production cycles in refining and jewellery manufacturing, during which adverse price movements may cause mark-to-market losses or inventory write-downs. In falling markets, digital-gold customers may redeem in large volumes — by physical delivery or cash settlement — precisely when underlying inventory is depreciating, compounding liquidity pressure and forcing liquidation or cash outflows at unfavourable realisations. The RHP also flags US 'Fair and Reciprocal Plan' tariffs. No significant price volatility or demand reduction materially impacting operations in the past three Fiscals.

strategy_growth.detail: Revenue is heavily concentrated in enterprise sales through the 'Augmont SPOT' platform plus the international sales business. The Company states the concentration exposes it to declines in demand for gold and silver bullion or jewellery from changes in consumer preferences, macroeconomic conditions, regulatory developments or shifts in investment behaviour. The RHP prints the absolute sum of all related party transactions as ₹457,141.31 million for FY26 against revenue from operations of ₹941,862.12 million, and states that no long-term agreements exist with any customer.

Customer concentration more than doubled at the top in one year: top-10 customers 36.63% (FY24), 35.72% (FY25) and 52.09% (FY26); top-5 29.43%, 28.89% and 46.32%; largest customer 12.17%, 11.90% and 27.44%. On the SPOT platform Maharashtra rose from 41.02% to 63.24% of platform revenue while Kerala fell from 6.13% to 0.87%. In the same year SPOT gold transaction counts fell 44.37% and silver counts 37.45% while SPOT revenue rose from ₹553,397.69 million to ₹817,505.69 million — fewer, far larger tickets, on the RHP's own tables.

FY26 net cash from operating activities was negative ₹421.57 million after ₹1,054.48 million and ₹967.39 million: cash generated from operations was ₹1,131.54 million and taxes paid net of refund ₹1,553.11 million. Net cash fell ₹867.21 million to a closing balance of ₹868.93 million. The working-capital lines swung hard both ways — other current liability ₹(9,381.07) million in FY26 against ₹+9,307.58 million in FY25, and other current and non-current assets ₹+8,705.35 million against ₹(9,362.08) million — and the RHP names no counterparty behind either leg.

The margin is a sliver and one non-operating line carries a large part of the profit. The RHP's own benchmarking prints FY26 gross margin 0.62%, EBITDA margin 0.41% and PAT margin 0.37%. Other income rose from ₹212.71 million to ₹962.56 million, including a gain on derivative financial instruments of ₹772.37 million — nil in FY25 and ₹2.02 million in FY24 — which MD&A attributes to profit on commodity futures. Because the RHP's own EBITDA definition subtracts other income, that gain sits outside the printed EBITDA of ₹3,859.50 million but inside PBT of ₹4,730.97 million, EPS, RoNW and RoCE; and the restated cash-flow statement's (Gain)/Loss on Derivative Financial Instrument add-back prints nil for FY26 against 16.36 for FY25.

Refining — the step that justifies the word integrated — is close to idle and shrinking. Chartered-engineer-certified utilisation (Chhibber and Associates, certificate dated August 17, 2026): Rudrapur 8.58% (FY24), 3.14% (FY25) and 0.93% (FY26), actual production 12.35, 4.52 and 1.34 MTPA against 144 MTPA installed; Mumbai 1.88%, 7.54% and 8.53%, production 2.63, 10.56 and 11.95 MTPA against 140 MTPA. Volume of gold refined fell to 13.34 MT in FY26 from 15.08 MT and 14.98 MT, and doré bars procured fell from 14.97 MT in FY24 to 10.78 MT — in the year revenue from operations grew from ₹662,307.79 million to ₹941,862.12 million. Subsidiary AIL's special warehouse licence application at Rudrapur was withdrawn by letter dated May 20, 2026 after roughly a year pending, and the premises vacated from May 1, 2026.

The core funding channel is closed by regulation, so what borrowing remains is callable. The Master Direction – RBI (Non-Banking Financial Company – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025 and the parallel 2025 Directions for commercial and co-operative banks prohibit advances for purchase of gold in any form; the Company states it therefore cannot access debt financing for gold stock-in-trade and has historically funded working capital through inter-corporate deposits and equity or preference infusions. As at June 30, 2026 the largest facility is unsecured inter-corporate deposits at subsidiary level — ₹173.45 million outstanding against ₹2,250.00 million sanctioned — at 9.00% per annum, perpetual from first disbursement and repayable with outstanding interest within 15 days of the lender's demand. No lender is named anywhere; the Financial Indebtedness statement is presented by category of borrowing.

The regulatory ground under the consumer business is unsettled and has already cost the Company partners. Material Subsidiary Augmont Goldtech Private Limited (revenue ₹66,885.22 million, 7.10% of revenue from operations in FY26) runs digital gold with no sector-specific approvals, registrations or licences; SEBI issued a public caution on dealing in Digital Gold on November 8, 2025; and the RHP discloses that certain partners have already terminated their agreements "pursuant to interventions from SEBI prohibiting trading members from offering digital gold, which is not a recognized security under Rule 8(3)(f) of the Securities Contracts Regulation Act, 1956". Because AGTPL is a B2C inventory-based e-commerce entity in which FDI is not permitted, the Company has capped foreign investment in itself at 49% by Board resolution dated June 12, 2025 and Shareholders' resolution dated June 13, 2025.

Demand-side policy moved against the product in the months before this RHP: import duty on gold and silver was raised from 6% to 15% in May 2026 (basic customs duty to 10% plus a 5% agriculture infrastructure and development cess), which the RHP says is likely to reduce import volumes, raise procurement cost, constrain working capital and suppress demand for bulk bullion purchases; and in the same month, per the RHP, "the Prime Minister of India publicly urged citizens to refrain from purchasing gold for a period of at least one year to reduce non-essential imports and conserve foreign exchange reserves". Imports also run under a DGFT restricted-item authorisation limited to typically 10 metric tonnes at once, valid 18 months.

The entire ₹4,650.00 million working-capital object rests on management estimates. The RHP states the fund requirements and deployment "have not been appraised by any external agency or any bank or financial institution or any other independent agency"; there are no firm arrangements of finance, the Company relying on Regulation 7(1)(e) because the objects are funded only from Net Proceeds and internal accruals; the long-term supply arrangements the proceeds would fund are ones the Company "may enter" with miners and refiners; any shortfall would be met from internal accruals and "additional debt from third party lenders other than scheduled commercial banks and NBFCs"; and the general corporate purposes amount is printed as a blank placeholder. The only certification is by M/s K.K. Mankeshwar and Co. as to derivation from the standalone financial statements (certificate dated August 17, 2026, UDIN 26156160HSXQNT8350).

Statutory-payment discipline is weak for an issuer of this size: FY26 shows 12 TDS instances of ₹2.04 million aggregating 2,168 delay-days (7 instances and 279 days in FY25; 9 and 494 in FY24), 9 provident fund instances and 9 EPS instances each aggregating 1,156 days, and 2 GST instances of 30 days; professional tax returns for Maharashtra for April 2025 to March 2026 could not be filed at all, attributed to portal issues, with no remediation date stated.

Service quality slipped as volumes rose: customer complaints and queries raised were 5,432 (FY24) and 3,667 (FY25) with 100% resolved, against 12,576 in FY26 of which 12,495 were resolved — 81 left open. The Company runs ₹941,862.12 million of revenue with 296 permanent employees and one contractual employee, on permanent-employee attrition of 25.68% (FY26), 114.66% (FY25, attributed to a transfer of employees to Finkurve) and 29.04% (FY24), and Senior Management attrition of 18.18%, 28.00% and 9.09%.

Much of the consumer-facing network is not the issuer's. Eleven of the 20 spot delivery centres are franchisee-operated; all 106 Gold-For-All centres are operated by Group Company Finkurve Financial Services Limited; the gold loans behind them are Finkurve's, with the Company earning only a service fee under the service level agreement dated June 26, 2024 — technology support revenue of ₹61.40 million in FY26, down from ₹83.63 million in FY24, the only consumer line that fell across the three Fiscals. Revenue from franchise, partner, associate and other channels is ₹28,698.22 million, 3.05% of revenue from operations.

International sales, the second vertical, went backwards: ₹80,521.67 million (12.16% of revenue from operations) in FY25 to ₹57,014.86 million (6.05%) in FY26, volume 11.52 MT to 6.63 MT — UAE ₹17,510.04 million, Hong Kong ₹30,529.25 million, Turkey ₹8,975.58 million. Jaipur unit utilisation fell from 77.87% to 47.07%. Two subsidiaries, Augmont Trading Limited and Augmont International Limited, printed nil revenue in each of the three Fiscals.

Supplier concentration rose alongside customer concentration and is bank-dependent: top-5 suppliers 46.88% (FY25) to 58.24% (FY26) of total materials procured and top-10 64.94% to 74.18%, with HDFC Bank Limited at 19.93% and Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited, Mumbai Branch at 18.28% in FY26. One FY25 top-10 supplier at 3.59% is anonymised for want of consent, which the RHP concedes "may limit investors' ability to fully assess the nature and extent of our supplier relationships or the pedigree of such suppliers".

The three Promoter Selling Shareholders offering ₹2,050.00 million (Namita Ketan Kothari ₹694.00 million, Vivek Prithviraj Kothari ₹694.00 million, Dimple Mukesh Kothari ₹662.00 million) carry a certified average cost of acquisition of ₹1.86 per Equity Share, and five other Promoters carry ₹0.00. The external marks in the document are secondary transfers at ₹40.15 per share to two sitting Directors on September 2 and 4, 2025, a private placement at ₹678.51 on August 29, 2025, and secondary sales at ₹991.00 per share between May 23 and 26, 2026 — under three months before this RHP. Ltd., Zaveri and Co., Sovereign Metals Ltd. and Safegold — every one of which is UNLISTED, with Fiscal 2026 printed as NA for all of them and no EPS, P/E, RoNW or NAV printed for any. EXTRACTION GAP, not RHP silence, on hedging quantum: the financial instruments note does disclose the policy — derivative contracts designated as fair value hedges against gold price movements, primarily commodity future contracts and forward foreign exchange contracts, governed by Board-approved principles — and prints the instrument headings for gold, silver and gold ETF, but the quantities in that table did not survive text extraction. The RHP contradicts itself in four places and reconciles none of them: FY26 SPOT gold volume sold 49.13 MT (Our Business) against 53.41 MT (MD&A); FY26 silver volume 1,033.57 MT against 1,049.05 MT; FY25 net cash from operating activities ₹1,054.48 million in the cash-flow table against ₹1,052.48 million in the narrative immediately beneath it; and the consumer measure, revenue from consumer-focused offerings at 7.10% of FY26 revenue against Augmont Gold For All platform revenue at 3.20% — both printed, neither described as a subset of the other.

Lab grown diamond trading was enabled on the SPOT platform in Fiscal 2026 but no revenue, volume or carat figure is printed for it; and the RHP prints no revenue-by-end-user-industry or customer-type split for any vertical.

red_flags: A Promoter Group entity is the counterparty to the largest revenue line, a top-five supply line and a two-way lending line at once. Riddisiddhi Bullions Limited in FY26: sales ₹258,474.29 million (27.44% of revenue from operations), purchases ₹59,539.72 million (6.36% of materials procured), loans given ₹67,418.75 million and received back ₹66,291.93 million, plus ₹199.26 million of cancellation-charge income. The RHP states that since no conflict of business interests arose in FY24 to FY26, "no agreements or arrangements have been entered into to manage any conflict of interest"; the only safeguards named are Audit Committee review and Board oversight.

The related party schedule prints ₹105.87 million of interest expense to Riddisiddhi Bullions Limited in FY26, while total finance costs in the restated consolidated statement of profit and loss for FY26 are ₹18.53 million. Both figures are the RHP's own and the document does not reconcile them.

Three sitting Directors appear on the RoC/MCA list of directors of struck-off companies — Whole-time Director Ketan Bhawarlal Kothari (eight companies, including Arvog Services Limited and Kentrico Enterprises IFSC Private Limited), Whole-time Director Mahendra Kumar Nemichand Bafna (two) and Independent Director Nishant Tolchand Ranka (one). Mr Bafna was additionally a director of Nem Textiles Private Limited, which filed form STK-2 on September 22, 2025 and awaits publication of strike-off.

Ideal Fiscal Services Limited, Augmont International Limited and Augmont Trading Limited were acquired at the face value of each equity share without obtaining valuation reports, and the RHP itself concedes such acquisitions "may be regarded as not being fully in compliance with applicable laws", with no assurance that the registrar of companies or other authorities will not take adverse action or impose penalties.

Securities-market history runs through the Promoter Group and touches the issuer. Riddisiddhi Bullions Limited was restrained by SEBI's interim order dated August 20, 2015 from dealing in the securities market in the illiquid stock options matter until April 5, 2018, and settled under the 2020 scheme (disposal orders dated January 14 and January 29, 2021). The Company, though not a party to that order, itself paid a settlement amount of ₹542,500 on October 21, 2020. Separately the DGFT fined Riddisiddhi Bullions Limited ₹1,000.00 million in January 2015 and revoked its nominated agency status over an alleged domestic sale of 200 kilos of gold — a matter still pending before the Bombay High Court, which the RHP states has no direct impact on the Company.

The Company's principal place of business was searched on January 10, 2019 by officers of CGST and Central Excise, Mumbai Central, in an investigation into alleged circular trading transactions involving gold bullion; the resulting show cause notice dated November 2, 2023 alleged wrongful availment of input tax credit of ₹1,141.99 million and wrongful passing on of ₹1,465.32 million. The proceedings were dropped in entirety on February 5, 2025, but Criminal Writ Petition No. 1309 of 2019 filed by the Company and Whole-time Director Ketan Bhawarlal Kothari seeking protection against arrest remains pending before the Bombay High Court.

A Company bank account at SBI, Nariman Point was frozen to the extent of ₹13.90 million in connection with FIR No. 0010 dated April 30, 2024 alleging a cyber fraud of ₹36.01 million, on the basis that ₹0.5 million of the fraudulently transferred monies reached the Company through layered accounts as consideration for a gold sale from M/s Chetan Jewellers; de-freezing was allowed only against a fixed deposit surety of ₹8.58 million, and the Company filed criminal revision petition 3693 of 2025 on June 12, 2025. A separate contingent liability line prints ₹15.25 million for balances attached by the bank for an alleged cyber incident involving a third party.

Statutory dues were paid late and by a wide margin: FY26 TDS 12 instances of ₹2.04 million aggregating 2,168 days, provident fund 9 instances and EPS 9 instances aggregating 1,156 days each, GST 2 instances of 30 days; and professional tax returns for Maharashtra for the whole of April 2025 to March 2026 could not be filed.

Documentation quality is thin at the top of the house: Promoter Dimple Vivek Kothari's prior work experience and Promoter and Senior Management Personnel Vivek Prithviraj Kothari's bachelor's degree are evidenced only by affidavit because relieving letters, degree certificates and independent third-party verification were unavailable, and the RHP states their accuracy, authenticity or completeness cannot be assured. Two Forms MGT-14 from February 2019 carried clerical errors and were re-filed after the prescribed period with delay fees.
strengths_observed: Scale and three-year trajectory as printed: revenue from operations ₹349,214.93 million (FY24) to ₹662,307.79 million (FY25) to ₹941,862.12 million (FY26), a CAGR of 64.23% the RHP itself prints; profit for the year ₹759.66, ₹2,271.88 and ₹3,483.00 million; basic and diluted EPS ₹9.08, ₹26.89 and ₹40.45; NAV per Equity Share ₹25.29, ₹52.21 and ₹111.00.

Returns and an almost debt-free balance sheet on the RHP's own figures: RoNW 43.98% / 69.47% / 49.52% (weighted average 55.25%), RoE 51.04% and RoCE 40.27% in FY26; total debt ₹126.72 million against shareholders' equity ₹9,068.89 million (printed debt-equity 0.01 in FY26 from 0.29 in FY24); current ratio 3.79 from 1.25. No Promoter shares are pledged, no issued shares are encumbered, and there are no outstanding options, warrants or convertibles.

The integration is physical, not asserted: two refining units (Rudrapur 144 MTPA, Mumbai 140 MTPA), a jewellery unit at Sitapur SEZ, Jaipur (13.80 MTPA), NABL ISO/IEC 17025:2017 assay laboratories with BIS hallmarking licences at both refineries, Authorised Economic Operator T-2 status, India Good Delivery certification, delivery rights on BSE- and MCX-operated commodity exchanges, and a GIFT City subsidiary trading directly on the IIBX — all as of March 31, 2026.

Distribution reach is measured rather than adjectival: 20 spot delivery centres across 13 states with orders 'typically fulfilled within two working days', 5,223 registered 'Augmont SPOT' members, 106 Gold-For-All centres against 60 in FY24, over 218 digital partners including Gullak and Candere, redemption at over 310 Kalyan Jewellers and over 130 CaratLane branches, 705 independent financial agents and over 49.62 million registered digital gold consumers.

Working capital turns fast for the capital employed: FY26 inventory days 1.33, trade receivable days 0.70 and trade payable days 0.27, with inventory turnover 275.45x and trade receivable turnover 518.26x — the RHP's own printed ratios.

Consumer engagement grew on printed volumes: 'Augmont Gold For All' transactions 28,479,217 (FY24) to 35,716,815 (FY25) to 54,934,891 (FY26); average transaction value ₹224.36, ₹331.35 and ₹548.29; platform revenue ₹6,389.65, ₹11,834.87 and ₹30,120.51 million.

The Fresh Issue is monitored and the largest historical legal exposure was extinguished before filing: CARE Ratings Limited is appointed Monitoring Agency under Regulation 41(1) with quarterly reporting until the Gross Proceeds are utilised in full, and the show cause notice dated November 2, 2023 alleging wrongful availment of input tax credit of ₹1,141.99 million and wrongful passing on of ₹1,465.32 million was dropped in its entirety by Order-in-Original dated February 5, 2025 for want of sufficient evidence.

Board and audit machinery were put in place ahead of the Offer: eight Directors of whom four are independent (including one woman director), all six committees constituted by Board resolution dated June 12, 2025, statutory auditor KKC & Associates LLP (peer review certificate 016960) appointed February 5, 2025, and insurance cover of ₹62,113.01 million as of March 31, 2026 against total assets (PP&E, CWIP, right-of-use assets and inventories) of ₹3,710.04 million — printed as 1,674.19%.

The RHP records affirmative nils on operating hygiene for the last three Fiscals: no theft, fraud or misappropriation instance, no IT or data-security incident, no hedging failure, no insurance claim filed, no shutdown from natural or man-made disaster, no loss of a key customer, and no failure to meet working capital requirements, repayment obligations or covenants.
